After a few weeks of travel, Mar'dy had arrived in the Forest of brotherhood, it really was something completely different. The forests he had gotten used to were unkept, fallen trees, vines and weeds made them look uninviting. You could spot an animal here and there, but this was completely different. The transition to the forest maintained by the Saen was somewhat of a gradual one but even an hour in it became very clear. The animals were more plentiful and friendly. There were no fallen logs or trees, fruit trees were plentiful and grew big juicy fruits instead of wild ones. The group stopped for a bit and foraged, refilling their supplies. But before they could depart, the captain of the Flora called the warriors to attention. One was singled out, Toki, who was to be first one to leave to meet the Thorac tribe, the most Eastern one settled in the Forest.

Sa'vak had trained them well. Toki stood proud and tall, receiving his assignment and bidding farewell to his fellows. He saluted to Mar'dy and Sa'vak and then left with in a brisk jog.

"Hmm. I wonder why no Saen have come to meet us. You would think they would notice the beetles." Mar'dy remarked.

"I suspect they have seen us. They may be a bit wary of the Flora, it wasn't long ago that problems had arisen between the Saen and obsessions of the Flora. But they will soon realize those dark days are passed." Saule replied.

"Yes, well we will let them come to us before we set off again, its evening anyway." Mar'dy said. Then he strolled away from the camp, sitting down on a rock. Pulling out the "Wonderful Things" journal he began to draw once more, as he had every evening on this journey. He drew the new fruits he had seen in the Forest and any new plants he hadn't seen before. Then he pulled out his map and began to calculate. The beetles were pretty wonderful in that unlike Landwalkers they always kept the exact same pace and always walked in straight lines. As if they simply couldn't walk any different. They were in fact not all that bright either and required to be manually steered away from obstacles.

This came in useful, based on which direction they were moving and how long they went for, Mar'dy could predict distances. The cartographer taught him all these tricks, though the math still took him a long time. He peered over his map. Unless he was wrong, the Forest of Brotherhood got bigger from when the map was made. By at least 20km in this direction. Well that would make sense, the Saen are constantly expanding, he concluded.

All the math had made him tired as well as the meal of fresh fruits he had while foraging. He stumbled back to the camp and and lay down beside his favourite beetle. The beetles didn't snore during the night but they did hum a little bit, an audible white noise. He curled up right beside the beetle and fell asleep. It reminded him of the ocean.

Sa'vak scowled, he had made three passes around the camp. The Flora were alert, but this jungle was horrid. A thing could sneak right up on you, right to your toes, and put a dagger in your heart. It's what he would have done. So much blasted cover. He looked over at Mar'dy, and wondered how he could sleep so well. So contented, so peaceful. It was a wonder he had survived so long. There was something special about his new brother, of that he was certain. Whatever Mar'dy touched, turned to gold. He had a spirit about him, a way of caring for others, a kind of innocence. Yes, that was it, an innocent soul. Sa'vak would be damned if he failed his new master.

He had drilled the Flora constantly, every minute they had a break. They were beginning to approach passable. He was drilling them in close formation fighting, it would be useful in this green hell. Still Sa'vak paced, it was better to be busy, than to think of the past. To think of his family and his failures. He would check the camp again, and then maybe a wider perimeter. Blasted jungle!

Mar'dy had been traveling for quite a while, but has now almost arrived at the Forest of Brotherhood. Sa'vak is still worried about the tactical position of being surrounded by insane amounts of cover. Pome calms Sa'vak's nerves.

One problem I see when it comes to modding pd2 is people are often unwilling to share what they know about the game code. So, if you want to share what you've learned post it in here. Post the code and a brief explanation of what the code does and anything else you want people to know. You can also ask for code examples here.

I'll get the ball rolling. This little piece of code, just 2 lines will allow you to jump as high as you want to and not take any fall damage.

Jump tweak_data.player.movement_state.standard.movement.jump_velocity.z = 50000

This will make it so you don't take any fall damage, otherwise you would die jumping that high. lol function PlayerDamage:damage_fall(data) end

I have the jump height set extremely high in this example. :) You'll probably want to lower that value a lot.

This code will unlock all the DLC for you, if you're into that kind of thing and don't want to mess with unlocker programs

function WINDLCManager:_verify_dlcs()

 for dlc_name, dlc_data in pairs(Global.dlc_manager.all_dlc_data) do

 dlc_data.verified = true

 end

end

Then, you just have to post Require to lib/managers/dlcmanager.
